 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao

Judgement:
The appellant is 3rd respondent, the respondents are claim petitioner and respondent Nos.1 and 2 in
M.V.O.P.No.223 of 2007 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional
District Judge, Krishna at Machilipatnam.

Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional
District Judge, Krishna at Machilipatnam

sentences.text: The appellant filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claim petitioner filed the petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident which took place on 13.11.2006 near Bandi Prasad poultry forms on Pamarru-Kuchipudi road.

4. The brief averments in the petition filed by the petitioner are as follows:
VGKR,J On 13.11.2006 at about 3.00 p.m. near Bandi Prasad poultry forms on Pamarru-Kuchipudi road, while the petitioner was proceeding on his two wheeler, a lorry bearing registration No.AIC 2529 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, as a result of which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The 1st respondent is driver, the 2nd respondent is owner and the 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle and hence, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. The 1st respondent did not resist the claim.
The 2nd respondent remained set ex parte.
The 3rd respondent/Insurance company filed a counter by denying the manner of the accident.
It is pleaded that the petitioner has to prove that the crime vehicle was insured with the Insurance company and the medical expenses incurred by him.

6. Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
VGKR,J 1) Whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle?

3) Whether the claim sought for by the petitioner and the interest are excessive 4) To what relief?
7. During the course of enquiry, on behalf of the petitioners, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A.1 to A.15 were marked and Exs.X.1 and X.2 were marked through P.W.2.
On behalf of the respondents, no evidence was adduced, however, a copy of the policy was got marked as Ex.B.1 8.
After considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim application and granted a sum of Rs.2,56,600/- towards compensation to the claimant.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the 3rd respondent-Insurance company has preferred the present appeal.
VGKR,J 9.
Heard arguments of learned standing counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the 1st respondent/claim petitioner.

10. The main two grounds, on which the present appeal is preferred by the appellant, are that the Tribunal failed to consider that the Ex.A.11-disability certificate indicates that there is no mention of permanent disability and that P.W.2 admitted that he cannot say whether the 35% disability is a functional disability or not.

11. Now, the points for determination are:
Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference?
12. POINT:

As can be seen from the impugned award, the Tribunal held that the driver of the crime vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident, due to that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The Tribunal further held that as is evident from Ex.B.1 that the crime vehicle was insured with the 3rd respondent/Insurance company and the 2nd respondent was its owner, both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
On considering the material on record, the learned Tribunal granted VGKR,J an amount of Rs.2,56,600/- towards compensation to the petitioner.
No appeal is filed against the said finding.
Therefore, this Court does not see any legal flaw or infirmity in the said finding recorded by the Tribunal.

13. As can be seen from the order of the Tribunal, the Tribunal calculated the future loss of earnings at Rs.2,01,600/- by relying on the evidence of P.W.2, who is a Medical Officer, and Ex.A.11- disability certificate that the disability of the petitioner is 35%.
But, a perusal of Ex.A.11 shows that there is no mention of permanent disability.
Further, P.W.2 deposed that he cannot say whether the disability of the petitioner is a functional disability or not.

Therefore, on considering the entire material on record, this Court arrive the disability of the petitioner at 30% instead of 35%
fixed by the Tribunal.
Here, the petitioner was aged 35 years by the date of the accident and the multiplier applicable to the age group of the petitioner is "16".

Therefore, the loss of future earnings of the petitioner can be estimated at Rs.1,72,800/-
VGKR,J (Rs.3,000/- x 12 x 30/100 x 16).
The learned Tribunal also awarded an amount of Rs.15,000/- towards medical expenses and Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Thus, in all, the claim petitioner is entitled compensation of Rs.2,27,800/-.

14. Learned standing counsel for the 3rd respondent/Insurance company fairly represented before the Court that there are no violations in the policy and the crime vehicle was insured with the Insurance company and the policy is also on force.
Therefore, respondent Nos.2 and 3 are liable to pay the compensation to the claim petitioner.
15. In view of the above reasons, the appeal is partly allowed.

The order dated 29.03.2011 passed by the Tribunal in M.V.O.P.No.223 of 2007 is modified by reducing the compensation of Rs.2,56,600/-
awarded by the Tribunal to Rs.2,27,800/-.
The order of the Tribunal in all other respects shall remain intact.
No order as to costs.
VGKR,J Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
